archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A 2-5 team that has outscored its opponents behind a top-three defense, but whose sputtering passing game and string of close losses have buried its record below its play.

report.headline: A top-three defense stuck at 2-5 by close losses and a broken passing game.
report.take:
Start with the contradiction. Tampa Bay is 2-5, yet it has scored 162 points and allowed 151, ranks 13th in net EPA, and its point differential implies 3.1 wins rather than two. The gap is close games. The Bucs have won just one of their one-score games (a .167 rate, 30th), and every loss so far has been a tight one. That is a team that has been unlucky and also poor at the end of games, and the luck part usually evens out.

What drives the play is a defense that is new for this franchise. After ranking 17th and 16th in EPA allowed in 2024 and 2025, Todd Bowles' unit is third, and second against the pass. It holds offenses' top receivers furthest under their usual output of anyone in the league and rarely gives up anything underneath. The offense went the other way. A unit that ranked fifth in EPA in 2024 is 28th, and 30th throwing the ball. That held through a quarterback shuffle: Baker Mayfield started the first three weeks, Jalon Daniels the next three, and Mayfield returned in Week 7. The line run-blocks well but has allowed 22 sacks, 30th in the league, and the passing EPA was deep in the red under both quarterbacks.

The numbers hide how the defense wins. It does not get home: pressure rate is 26th and the missed-tackle rate is 30th. It wins with tight coverage and takeaways, and 11 of those (third) is a figure that tends to cool. Week 7's 43-13 rout of Carolina also flatters the offense. The Bucs threw for 64 yards and ran for 258 behind four takeaways. That is a blueprint for beating a struggling opponent, not proof the passing game is fixed.

Where it heads depends on the division as much as anything. Atlanta leads the NFC South at 3-4, Carolina is 3-3, and the Bucs are one game back with four division games left. Their underlying profile is the best in the group. The problem is timing: the starting tackle, the top receiver and the best safety are all on this week's report.

strengths.title: Coverage that smothers the short game
strengths.body: Tampa allows almost nothing on the short, timing throws most offenses live on, and it takes away the opponent's lead receiver. This comes from the secondary rather than the rush, which is why it has held up without much pressure. The one soft spot is the deep ball, where the Bucs are only league-average. Coverage-driven defenses are fairly stable, but losing Antoine Winfield Jr. tests the depth.

strengths.title: A run game that actually works
strengths.body: Bucky Irving has carried 120 times behind a line that gets him past the line of scrimmage. The run EPA is near break-even, which is good for a rushing offense, and yards per carry rank fifth. It is what has kept the offense afloat and the clock moving: the Bucs rank fourth in time of possession, which also shields the defense. Because the run blocking is real and not just game script, this should last.

strengths.title: Hidden yards: special teams, takeaways
strengths.body: A top-ten special teams unit and a ball-hawking defense keep handing a limited offense extra possessions and shorter fields. The Carolina blowout was built on exactly that. Special teams value is reasonably sticky. The takeaway pace is less so and should drift back.

concerns.title: The passing game is broken
concerns.body: This is the real flaw, not a product of role or game script. The passing EPA is 30th, the sack rate is 28th, and it was bad under both Mayfield and Daniels. The low point was the Pittsburgh loss, when Daniels' passing game cost more than 21 points of EPA. Coming off a top-five offense in 2024, there is talent to rebound, but the protection has to improve first.

concerns.title: No pass rush, shaky tackling
concerns.body: The defense is elite despite generating little pressure and missing tackles at one of the league's worst rates. That leaves it dependent on coverage holding and on takeaways continuing. Without a rush, the deep ball is where it can be hurt, and a missed tackle is how a short completion becomes a long one. It is a cost of the coverage-first style, but a real vulnerability.

concerns.title: Injuries at three load-bearing spots
concerns.body: Luke Goedeke played every snap at tackle, Winfield played nearly every snap at safety, and Emeka Egbuka leads the team in targets. All three are listed out. Losing a starting tackle hits the protection weakness directly, and losing Egbuka thins out a passing game that was already struggling. The return estimates suggest these are short-term, but even short absences cost a team chasing a division from 2-5.

trend.note: The pattern has barely moved: a defense that held up every week, a passing game that rarely did, and a run of close losses. The two wins came when the run game took over, peaking with Week 7's 258 rushing yards at Carolina.

nextGame.headline: Run the ball, trust the coverage, survive without Goedeke up front
nextGame.body:
This is a matchup of two run-first teams, and the Book has Tampa a 2.5-point home favorite. Atlanta's offense is built on the ground: it ranks sixth in rush EPA behind a line that rarely gets stuffed, and it passes well below expectation. Michael Penix Jr., starting since Week 3, leads a passing game that ranks 26th in EPA, which plays straight into Tampa's coverage. Atlanta's defense is middling but leaky against lead backs and in the red zone, and its special teams rank 29th. Atlanta has also yet to win a one-score game, so whichever side's close-game luck turns finally gets a chance here.

The Bucs list Goedeke, Winfield and Egbuka as out, and linebacker Christian Rozeboom is on injured reserve in a reserve role. Atlanta's list is long too. Linebacker Divine Deablo (83% of snaps) is out, as are cornerbacks Avieon Terrell and Billy Bowman Jr., who each played about half the snaps. That thins a secondary that has been good against deep throws. Running back Brian Robinson Jr., receiver Olamide Zaccheaus and tackle Michael Jerrell are also out.

waysToWin.title: Feed Irving against a soft run front
waysToWin.body: Atlanta has been one of the worst defenses against opposing lead backs on a per-play basis. Tampa's run blocking is a genuine strength. Leaning on Irving also keeps a protection unit missing Goedeke out of obvious passing downs, and it repeats the formula that worked at Carolina.

waysToWin.title: Make Penix win through the air
waysToWin.body: Atlanta's passing offense is 26th in EPA, and Tampa's pass defense is second, smothering underneath. Atlanta gets the ball out quickly, so the Bucs' lack of pressure matters less. If Tampa sells out against the run and forces third-and-long, Atlanta has shown little ability to throw its way out of trouble.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden-yardage battle
waysToWin.body: Special teams is a clear mismatch: Tampa ranks seventh and Atlanta 29th. Atlanta's defense also lets opponents score touchdowns on two-thirds of red-zone trips. Short fields and red-zone touchdowns can carry a Tampa offense that won't win many through the air.

waysToLose.title: Protection collapses without Goedeke
waysToLose.body: Tampa's sack rate was already near the bottom of the league with its full line. Atlanta's defense hits the quarterback at a top-ten rate. If drives keep dying on sacks, as they did in the Week 6 loss to Pittsburgh, the run game never gets enough snaps to matter.

waysToLose.title: Atlanta's run game meets missed tackles
waysToLose.body: Atlanta's ground game is its best weapon. Tampa's run defense is strong by EPA, but its tackling ranks 30th, and Winfield's absence removes a sure-handed last line. Long Atlanta drives would flip the time-of-possession edge the Bucs rely on.

waysToLose.title: Another close one slips away
waysToLose.body: Both teams have struggled to close tight games. For Tampa, the losses have often come through turnovers, like the four in the Week 1 loss to Cincinnati. Without Egbuka and with Atlanta strong against deep throws, the Bucs have little big-play margin to recover from a giveaway.

nextGame.watch: How Tampa protects Mayfield with Goedeke out. If the replacement holds up, the run game and coverage should carry the day; if not, this becomes another one-score coin flip.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense is the part to trust. It is coverage-based, it has been consistent every week, and it should keep games close. Expect the takeaway count and the bad luck in close games to drift back toward normal, which favors Tampa: a team with a positive point differential rarely keeps losing this many coin flips. The run game is sustainable too. What caps the ceiling is a passing game that has been bottom-three all year, and losing a starting tackle and the top target won't help in the short term.

The schedule offers a path. Four division games remain in a division whose leader is 3-4, plus the winless Chargers at home and Detroit, whose defense ranks 31st. Chicago, Baltimore and the Rams will be harder. If Mayfield's return steadies the passing game even to below average, this team can climb back to around .500 and compete for the NFC South. If it doesn't, the defense keeps games close and the record keeps undershooting the play.
swingFactors: Pass protection while Goedeke is out

confidence.note: Seven games, a quarterback shuffle and fresh injuries to key starters
